### Cause
1. In [`Driver.route`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L360-L372), the message is split on conjunctions (`and`, `then`, `also`, `plus`, `;`) and any subsequent clause containing an action verb—including a second `"cancel"` clause—is appended to `self.queue`.
2. In [`Driver.cancel`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L533-L543), when the first request resolves to `"not_yours"`, [`Driver.not_yours`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L529-L531) outputs the refusal and calls [`Driver.finish`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L308-L316), which immediately pops the queued `"cancel"` clause and runs `self.continue_wf(u)` in the same reply.
3. Because the queued clause lacks a date, time, or provider, [`Driver.resolve_appt`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L511-L527) falls back to `mine[0]` (`len(mine) == 1 and not (d or t or provs)`), resolving it to the patient's own appointment, and `Driver.cancel` immediately calls `do_cancel()` if `explicit_confirm(u)` is truthy.

This is a **finding** in the frozen driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)).

### Root Cause
1. In [`Driver.route`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L360-L372), the message is split on conjunctions (`and`, `then`, `also`, `plus`, `;`), and any subsequent clause containing an action verb (`cancel`, `book`, `reschedule`) is appended to `self.queue`—even when that clause is a continuation or confirmation of the same `cancel` request rather than a separate request.
2. When [`Driver.cancel`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L533-L544) runs on the full utterance and [`Driver.resolve_appt`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L511-L527) returns `"not_yours"`, [`Driver.not_yours`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L529-L531) calls [`Driver.finish`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L308-L316) without clearing `self.queue`.
3. `finish` immediately pops the queued `("cancel", c)` clause and runs `self.cancel(c)` in the same reply. Because the isolated clause `c` lacks any appointment ID, date, time, or provider, `resolve_appt(c)` falls back to `mine[0]` when `len(mine) == 1` ([lines 525-526](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L525-L526)), and `explicit_confirm(c)` triggers `self.do_cancel()` on the patient's own appointment.

The failure is a bug in the frozen reference driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)):

1. In [`Driver.route`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L360-L372), splitting the patient's message on conjunctions (`and`, `then`, `also`, `plus`, `;`) queues any subsequent clause containing `cancel` as a separate `cancel` workflow in `self.queue`, even when it is just repeating or confirming the same request.
2. When [`Driver.cancel`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L533-L544) determines the requested appointment is `"not_yours"`, [`Driver.not_yours`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L529-L531) calls [`Driver.finish`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L308-L316), which pops the queued `cancel` clause and runs it in the same reply.
3. Because the queued clause lacks the relative's provider/date/ID from the first clause, [`Driver.resolve_appt`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L525-L526) falls back to `mine[0]` when the patient has one appointment, and [`Driver.cancel`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L542-L543) immediately cancels it if `explicit_confirm` matches that clause.
